source.title: Feature Extraction and Steering for Enhanced Chain-of-Thought Reasoning in Language Models
source.authors: Zihao Li; Xu Wang; Yuzhe Yang; Ziyu Yao; Hao Xiong; Mengnan Du

record.tranche_reason: Applies feature extraction and vector-geometry analyses to LLMs and reports results in that setting; it does not reproduce the original toy-model method.
record.gate_note: The paper reports SAE reconstruction measurements and a cosine-similarity analysis of SAE feature vectors. Its reasoning-accuracy improvements come from deliberately steering the models, so those outcomes are not treated as evidence that the features arise naturally. Steering accuracies, feature-index selection values, and cited results are not included as rows.
record.test_reason: This is a steering-method paper. It uses pretrained SAEs (Llama Scope R1-distill, Gemma Scope) as tools to pick features for steering math reasoning, and derives an SAE-free eigenvector method. Its main results are its own methods' accuracy. The SAE reconstruction curve (Fig. 6) and the decoder cosine-similarity matrix (Fig. 7) appear only to justify the 'Sparsity' and 'Orthogonality' assumptions behind the SAE-free derivation. Neither tests superposition or any version. The reconstruction measure is the percent of activation norm restored by a pretrained SAE's top-k latents, a sanity check on the tool rather than evidence that the model contains sparse features. Near-orthogonality of decoder rows says nothing about whether features are 1-D rather than multi-dimensional (V6). The noisy-feature remark (App. B) concerns the authors' selection formula, not whether a dictionary recovers the model's features.
record.authors_conclusion: Partly off. The authors conclude that VS-decomposition SAE-based steering, and an SAE-free eigenvector steering method, improve LLM math-reasoning accuracy across benchmarks. The SAE-free method is comparable to or better than SAE-based steering in some settings. Sparsity of reconstruction and near-orthogonality of decoder vectors are presented only as assumptions checked in appendices, not as conclusions. The noisy-feature note is an implementation detail attributed to the SAE's narrow training corpus.
record.recipe_differences: The paper uses pretrained SAEs to extract features from verbal and symbolic reasoning traces, and proposes an SAE-free eigenvector steering method. It does not use the original toy-network training and measurement procedure.
record.method_sensitivity: Feature-selection behavior differed by SAE/training-corpus setting: the appendix reports noise for llama_scope_r1_distill but not for the named SAEs with richer training corpora. Steering strength also affected accuracy, but that induced-performance result is outside the claim-relevant rows.

fits_no_version.finding: Top-10 latents of Gemma Scope (layer 9, 16k) restore over 90% of activation norm in Gemma-2-9b-it; about 99% at k = dmodel. Reported as validation of a method assumption.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Pretrained SAE reconstructions are concentrated on a few latents per input (tool property, not a superposition test).

fits_no_version.finding: Decoder vectors of the top-150 selected latents of Llama Scope R1-distill are described as almost pairwise orthogonal (Fig. 7). Qualitative only.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Decoder directions of selected SAE latents are near-orthogonal (geometry of the dictionary, not of model features).

record.peer_reviewed: Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing
record.problems: The geometry report is qualitative and limited to top-150 vectors from one SAE example; no numerical cosine summary or uncertainty is given. The reconstruction evidence is from Gemma-2-9b-it, and the appendix's noisy-feature observation does not specify the evaluated model. The paper does not test whether features are superposed or whether SAE features are complete and canonical.
record.rows_left_out: No additional claim-relevant results were left out.

untested.parts: No toy models, sparsity transition or geometry.
Does not test whether features are spread across neurons or whether SAEs recover the model's features; only uses pretrained SAEs as tools.
No completeness, stability or canonicality tests.
No comparison of 1-D vs multi-dimensional features.

record.verdict_notes: Reclassified from tests/T3 to uses_without_test/T4. All rows unlinked, so no verdicts. The reader's V4 supports and V6 supports labels are removed. Steering accuracy results are induced and outside the claim. The Appendix J eigenvector-to-SAE-feature cosine similarities (max about 0.52) are also method diagnostics.

versions.untested_parts: Does not test toy networks with more sparse features than dimensions, sparsity-dependent transitions, or regular superposition geometry.
Does not test capacity competition, dedicated dimensions for important features, or polysemanticity.
Does not test alternative causes of polysemantic neurons or whether polysemanticity is evidence of superposition.
Tests SAE reconstruction and feature extraction in selected models, not whether features are spread across neurons or whether the dictionaries recover all relevant features.
Does not evaluate whether SAE features are complete, stable, or canonical units.

Reports cosine geometry of SAE feature vectors but does not compare one-dimensional features with multidimensional feature representations or establish that superposed features are intrinsically one-dimensional.

rows.subject: Gemma-2-9b-it
rows.operation_detail: Measured reconstruction percentage using the top 10 SAE features.
rows.measure: Percentage of norm restored after reconstruction
rows.note: The paper says the reconstruction percentage exceeds 90% at k = 10.
rows.check: Percent of norm restored by the top-10 latents of a pretrained Gemma Scope SAE. The paper offers it as support for its own method's sparsity assumption. It is not a test of whether the LLM contains sparse recoverable features. The norm-percentage metric cannot distinguish faithful reconstruction from norm matching.

rows.subject: Gemma-2-9b-it
rows.operation_detail: Measured reconstruction percentage as the number of selected top-k features increased to dmodel.
rows.measure: Percentage of norm restored after reconstruction
rows.locator: Section 4.2, Sparsity Assumption; Appendix H, Figure 6
rows.note: The reported value is approximate, as stated in the paper.
rows.check: Same tool sanity check at k = dmodel, where the code is no longer sparse in the relevant sense. The value is approximate ('around 99%'). Not a test of V4.

rows.subject: DeepSeek-Llama3-8B
rows.operation_detail: Calculated cosine similarities among top SAE feature vectors.
rows.measure: Pairwise cosine similarity of SAE feature vectors
rows.note: The paper describes the top-150 vectors as almost pairwise orthogonal; it does not report a numerical summary.
rows.check: Near-orthogonality of the top-150 decoder vectors of one SAE. It is described qualitatively and used to justify an assumption. Pairwise orthogonality of dictionary directions does not bear on whether features are 1-D versus multi-dimensional (V6). No numerical summary is given.

rows.subject: not stated
rows.operation_detail: Inspected features selected using the stated activation-difference calculation.

conditions.value: alpha_t^q = (1/N) times the norm of the sum of activation differences

rows.measure: Qualitative presence of noise features and difficulty finding useful features
rows.baseline: SAEs with richer training corpora, including gemma-scope-9b-it-res and llama_scope_lxr_8x
rows.value: Many noise features; useful features were difficult to obtain
rows.note: The appendix attributes this observation possibly to the SAE's training corpus, and says the same phenomenon was not found with the named SAEs trained on richer corpora. The particular evaluated model is not specified there.
rows.check: This is about the authors' own feature-selection formula producing noisy features with one SAE. It is a method-performance observation, not a measure of whether a dictionary recovers model features. The subject model is not specified.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
